answer.rationale: Primary contract expires in 14 days with no auto-renew while the line sits at 94% and no buffer, so any action that changes the supplier or leaves coverage open would raise delivery risk. Inherited notes suggest staying with the incumbent avoided integration and delivery breaks, while renewal-window benchmarking and longer-term volume commitments previously recovered margin without shrinking service. That combination is the only path that can pursue the mandated spend cut without a supplier change. Unverified: whether an 18% reduction is actually achievable, whether those past concession patterns still hold, and what happens if talks fail before day 14. Deferral, a primary switch, and a new second source are set aside for now because they either assume month-to-month continuity this contract may not have or introduce onboarding risk the buffer cannot absorb.
